follow-up time: Through pregnancy and delivery, with offspring followed up for their first year of life
outcome: Pregnancy complications (e.g., pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, perinatal hemorrhage)
Offspring complications (e.g., low birth weight, low Apgar score, need for CPAP or NICU, congenital malformations, osteogenesis imperfecta, birth-related fractures, hospital contacts)
cohort: 433 pregnancies where either the mother (n=134) or father (n=73) had osteogenesis imperfecta, compared to a reference population of pregnancies in the general Danish population.
finding: Pregnancies with one parent having osteogenesis imperfecta had similar rates of pregnancy and delivery complications compared to the general population, with a higher rate of cesarean section.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rate was higher in the OI cohort (31%) than in the reference population (19%).
birth_weight: Low birth weight was studied as an outcome.
